tooth_t3_audit.flaw_locus: Tooth assertion used OR instead of substantive invariance: (probe_eval in fwd OR probe_eval in rev)
tooth_t3_audit.substantive_finding: Reversing candidate presentation order altered the selected top-2 candidate set, causing probe_eval (the sole advancing candidate) to be dropped in forward order and selected in reverse order. This is a severe substantive order-sensitivity failure.
tooth_t3_audit.gate_impact: Revokes Phase-2 authorization automatically under frozen contract.

needle_vs_random.finding: Needle pays 22.4 seconds of inference latency to produce 0.87 fewer successful horizons than random expectation.

pareto_dominance.reasons: Random achieves higher horizon success (61.7% vs 56.2%) and lower total wall-clock (23,428 ms vs 45,826 ms) with zero inference latency overhead. Needle is strictly dominated on operational success and payment.

claim_p1_pruning_signal.evidence: Recall advantage (+5.6%) is within 0.53 std of random (p = 0.3503); horizon success is worse than random expectation (56.2% vs 61.7%).

claim_p2_search_payment_reduction.evidence: Meaning A (vs exhaustive): +5,113.7 ms saved. Meaning B (vs cheaper alternatives): FAILED. Needle costs 5,091.8 ms/success (higher than exhaustive at 3,183.8 ms and 2.14x higher than random at 2,374.4 ms). Dominated by random.

claim_p3_incremental_value.evidence: Mechanically satisfied weak gate (7 > 5), but exact binomial test shows p = 0.3872 and 95% CI [-29.5%, +54.5%]. Statistically indistinguishable from chance.

authorization_reconciliation.original_frozen_gate_result: PASS (Mechanically fired under weak conditions and flawed T3 assertion)
authorization_reconciliation.developmental_defect_note: The original gate suffered from three defects: (1) Tooth T3 assertion permitted substantive order reversal; (2) P1 gate evaluated useful_recall alone, ignoring that Needle lost to random on horizon_success; (3) P3 gate used uncalibrated count comparison (7 > 5) without statistical discordance control.
